Subject: Mid-cycle capacity bump + co-term request

Hi Chloe,

Quick note from our side — we had an unexpected product win and need to increase our committed capacity by ~30% starting June 1. We want to align the new capacity so it co-terms with our existing annual contract that renews Feb 1, 2028.

Procurement asked whether Redwood can: 1) apply a partial credit for the unused portion of our current commitment, and 2) offer a one-time uplift discount for the remainder of this contract term in exchange for the additional committed spend now.

We're on a tight timeline to finalize procurement paperwork by May 12. Can you outline options (pricing and any operational caveats) and whether you need a PO or a signed amendment? Happy to loop in our legal if helpful.

Thanks,
Maria

VeroHealth

Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity bump + co-term request

Hi Maria — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the win. Happy to get this moving quickly. A few clarifying Qs so we propose a clean path:

- Do you want the additional 30% to be reserved capacity (guaranteed throughput) or an add-on bucket that can burst?
- Is the target start date firm (June 1) or flexible by a week or two?
- Can you confirm current monthly usage from the attachment so I can model prorated credits precisely?

High-level options we can offer this week:
1) Prorated top-up + co-term: add the 30% as a pro-rated commitment for the remainder of the Feb 1, 2028 term. We apply a one-time partial credit for unused current committed capacity proportional to remaining term.
2) Immediate uplift + performance credit: add capacity now with a small upfront uplift discount (5–8% depending on absolute volume) and a quarterly performance credit if usage stays above threshold.
3) Staged voucher approach: convert some of the existing committed dollars into usage vouchers you can consume over the remainder of the term; new committed capacity starts now and co-terms.

I'll put a concrete numeric proposal together once you confirm the three bullets above. If helpful I can also draft an amendment for legal to review that only requires a PO for fast procurement.

I copied Ben (pricing) and Lauren (account lead) to weigh in on commercial and billing implications.

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Mid-cycle capacity bump + co-term request (internal)

Ben / Lauren / Neha — forwarding Maria's ask. Timeline: procurement wants to lock by May 12. Key constraints: co-term to Feb 1, 2028 and they'd like a partial credit for unused commit. They want a one-time uplift discount in exchange for increasing committed spend today (~30% uplift to committed GPU hours).

My initial thoughts:
- Offer structure: reduced uplift discount for shorter remaining term. For ~9 months remaining, suggest 6% uplift discount on incremental capacity if they commit now and co-term.
- Credit math: we should credit unused committed dollars pro-rata based on remaining months; avoid converting into negative invoices (use voucher stack).
- Operational: we can enable immediate reserved pools but flag that autoscaling buffer is limited for the first 30 days until capacity is warmed. Add a performance credit clause (0.5% of monthly spend) if we miss P95 latency SLA for two consecutive months.

Questions for pricing: Ben — can we go to 8% on uplift if they take a 12-month post-renewal extension instead of just co-term? Lauren — are we comfortable with voucher accounting versus direct invoice credits? Neha — will this require any changes to billing pipeline or billing codepaths for vouchers?

Thanks — Chloe

Hi Maria — appreciate the quick answers on the call this morning. Per our conversation, please find our recommended approach below and an attached amendment draft for review.

Summary proposal (option selected: Prorated top-up + co-term):
- Incremental committed capacity: +30% starting June 1, 2027 (reserved pool).
- Pricing on incremental capacity: list price less 6% uplift discount (applies to incremental committed spend for the remainder of the term).
- Credit for unused current commit: pro-rated voucher equal to unused months * committed monthly rate, applied to invoices through Feb 1, 2028. Vouchers are non-refundable and do not change the committed volumes.
- SLA and operational caveat: immediate capacity will be provisioned; we recommend a 30-day warm-up window where autoscale headroom is limited. If we miss P95 latency SLA for two consecutive months, we will issue a 0.5% monthly spend performance credit for each impacted month.
- Procurement paperwork: we can accept a PO referencing Amendment #A-VH-089 or a signed DocuSign amendment. For speed, a PO + emailed signed amendment summary is fine.

Next steps:
1) Maria / Procurement: confirm start date (firm for June 1?) and provide final PO by May 12.
2) VeroHealth legal: review attached amendment; we can tighten voucher language if needed.
3) Internal: Ben + Neha will prepare billing entries and voucher issuance steps once PO received.

I attached the pricing appendix and the amendment draft: redwood-uplift-proposal-v2.pdf. I'll also create the DocuSign envelope if you prefer the signature flow.

Thanks again — we can jump on a 15-min call to finalize details if that helps.

Best,
